description: Device session (protocols/mgcommands.h, Device session). Hex strings are Control payloads (write: client -> device, notify: what the device sends back, in order; an empty list means nothing). Every exchange starts on a new connection at the given ATT MTU with the given device flags (default: holds a token, proof matched, encrypted). The device holds test_credentials (test_credentials_bound when its flags have vm_binding) and sends them after its hello (as written there, keys in that order), answers hello with device_hello, registers node_id with test_commands as commands_v2 and is_wakeup_supported true (it handles wake), and answers each command with its test_payload. While a task is active (device flag task, event task: a user action, traffic it owes, a wait, a wake), after a state it didn't ask for (closed, no_network) it sends open_request [1] at once, then backs off (timed, not shown; closed and no_network run separate series, capped at 60 s and 15 s); an open restarts a series only after a session that stayed open 60 s; a closed or no_network after connecting (a failed open) counts the same; with no task it asks nothing, and none after not_enrolled, auth_failed or too_large until a new hello, a credentials_update or an open. Credentials leave and are taken only sealed (mgcommands.h, Sealed credentials, Sealed data): every unsealed hello is refused insecure, and every session is sealed under session_seal's K and proof nonces with node_id; a step with event proof is a new matching token proof with the nonces it lists (the session reset at its challenge), the keys for every sealed hello after it. A new proof, and every sealed hello, drop each sealed message part way in or out and restart the counters, so nothing from the old session completes in the new one or gives one of its counters back. The credentials are fake. Generated by mg_session_ref.py.

display.card.description: Show a card on the home screen: a title and a body.

mic_gate.description: The microphone gate (mgcommands.h, start_mic). Each step is a write (client -> device), a token proof (proof, as in exchanges) or an event on the gadget (press: its talk control; wake_word: a wake word it heard itself; console_press: the console's press word; charger: a charger plugged in; console_capture: a console word that starts capture, source wireless or wired, with the console's answer in console; time: its clock moves ms; reconnect: a new link), with what the device notifies and whether it captures afterwards (mic). Each exchange starts on a new connection whose token proof matched, unless its device flags have proof false; release false is an automation build; holds_token false is a device that isn't set up (a release one answers start_mic proof_required). The device captures SBC at 16 kHz and holds the session's test_credentials.

settings.description: Settings from a central without the token proof (mgcommands.h, set_settings). Steps as in streams_and_updates; each step also records flash, how many times the device has written its persisted settings so far; the event setup_complete ends Link setup on a device that held no token. The device lists push_to_talk_enabled, haptics_enabled and link_mode (per connection), audio_codec, speaker_volume, led_brightness and capture_sample_rate (persisted) and client_app, and takes the clock's device actions (set_unix_time, get_unix_time); the time is never refused for want of the proof. The device flag clock_floor is a device that refuses a time before 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z (a device may); every device refuses one after 9999-12-31T23:59:59Z. On a release build (the default) a device that holds a token answers the owner's content (client_name, client_app, the time) only after this connection's proof or in its local window; release false is a test build, which reads them back unproven. An exchange whose device flags say local_window true needs a device whose key hold opens a local window; a device without one (it answers the owner's content only to the proof) skips it.

proof_gates.description: More of the protocol behind the token proof (mgcommands.h, Token proof; README.md, Gadget setup v2). Steps as in streams_and_updates; each also records acted: the usages the device's HID pressed, the client's haptic pattern playing (its id) and the assistant_state shown. The device lists ui_input hid_key (its HID host connected), mg_command_skill with mg-skills-v2.json's test_skills, test_payloads and test_manifest, haptic_play and haptic_stop (a pattern plays until stopped; haptic_play is refused, reason disabled, until the client writes haptics_enabled 1 with set_settings on that connection, which is taken without the proof) and assistant_state; device flags hid, skills or haptics false leave that part out. Event resetup_request is a pairing_client_hello in Link setup on this device; setup is its answer: confirm_required (encrypted, once the handshake has its keys) or error_operation_in_progress (at once, in plaintext: plaintext is its bytes on the setup TX characteristic), and prompt what it did to the re-setup prompt (shown, taken_over: still on screen, bound to this hello, no new flash; none). Event dismiss is the back gesture (a swipe or a separate back key); event press while the prompt is up is the confirm key or a tap on the Confirm disc, which confirms it, or with key talk the talk key, which on a set-up release device only dismisses a re-setup prompt (a dismiss on its connection) and otherwise confirms; event tap_elsewhere (a tap outside the disc) changes nothing. Event setup_mode: the device restarts in setup mode (its button held at boot, into its normal firmware with Link setup under its normal identity; never a SAFE) and the phone reconnects; setup mode ends at the confirmed re-setup or setup_mode_ms after that boot (test and bench builds are always in it). Device flag talk_key_only: its only key is its talk key; on a release build it takes a re-setup only in setup mode, answering a hello outside it error_pairing_unavailable (in plaintext, no session). resetup, on those events: the connection and hello (counted from 1 on each connection) the prompt is bound to (null: none up) and those the last press confirmed. A resetup_request step may carry conn, the connection it arrives on when several are open (default 1), and invalid true: a hello whose top-level fields are valid but whose mobile_pub or mobile_nonce fails validation (error_pairing_invalid_hello; on the prompt's own connection it ends the prompt, prompt ended; device flags bad_hello_encrypted, the refusal encrypted under the session still current instead of in plaintext, and bad_hello_drops_link, the link dropped after it, work like dismiss_drops_link). Event setup_ends (with conn) is that connection's confirmed setup ending: its provision_v2 committed (auth_ok) or its session ended; until then other connections' hellos are refused too. Device flag dismiss_drops_link (default false): a device whose dismiss ends the setup link runs the exchanges flagged true and skips those flagged false, and the other way round; an exchange without the flag holds for both. An smp step is an SMP v1 request to the update gate of mg-update-v2.json (mg_update_ref.py's model) with the rc it answers and update_prompt after it (none or confirm); a press while the update prompt shows answers only that prompt's upload. Event injected_press is a console or Nordic UART word or a scripted tap: it confirms neither prompt.

exchanges.name: re-ask after an unasked end at MTU 247
